Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's HIPAA discovery call

Hi Sarah,

Great to meet you virtually today — appreciate the clear recap. Below is a summary and proposed next steps. I've attached a draft BAA and a short deployment matrix that maps eligibility to PHI handling.

Summary / answers to your questions:
- BAA availability: Redwood provides BAAs for Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Our hosted public API is not eligible to process PHI and cannot be covered by a BAA.
- Eligible deployment modes for PHI: Dedicated (customer-dedicated capacity) and Private (VPC or on-prem).
- PHI handling boundaries: PHI must only be sent to environments covered by the BAA (i.e., Dedicated or Private). In those modes we support:
  - Customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM) for data at rest
  - Audit logs and request-level traceability
  - Configurable retention policies and the ability to purge data on request
  - Option to disable persistent KV/prefix caching for sensitive workloads
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report; we can share the report under NDA.

Attachments I'm including: Redwood_BAA_Draft_v1.pdf and HIPAA_deployment_matrix.xlsx.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please upload the completed security questionnaire; we'll have our security team respond within 3 business days for scoped items.
2) Technical deep-dive: Dev Patel (cc'd) can do a 45-minute session to go over integration details and our deployment options. Availability: Thu 3/21 10:00-12:00 PST or Fri 3/22 14:00-16:00 PST.
3) If the BAA language looks close, legal can run a short review and revert redlines (we can also start an NDA if you prefer).

Let me know which time works and we'll lock it in.

Thanks,

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-03-21T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Technical clarifications re: PHI boundaries and deployment configurations

Hi Sarah,

Following up with a few technical clarifications from the infra side based on questions in the questionnaire: 

1) Hosted public API (redwood.com API): NOT eligible for PHI. Requests that include PHI cannot be routed through our multi-tenant public endpoints and are explicitly excluded from BAAs.

2) Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools that we provision for a single customer. When Dedicated is configured under a BAA we can:
   - Enforce network isolation and IP allowlists
   - Integrate with customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) for model and data encryption at rest
   - Provide request-level audit logs and longer retention of logs for audits
   - Offer an option to disable persistence of model KV cache across requests (recommended for sensitive data)

3) Private (VPC / on-prem): For customers that require full network control or air-gapped deployments we provide a private control plane and customer-managed infrastructure. This is the most flexible from a PHI-control perspective (on-prem can be configured to never allow egress to Redwood-managed storage).

4) Data flows to watch for: embeddings and conversation transcripts are common PHI vectors. If you plan to compute embeddings over PHI, those requests must go to Dedicated or Private with KMS enabled and caching disabled.

5) Evidence & timelines: We can produce configuration docs (network diagrams, key management notes) and scoped screenshots for the SOC 2 controls under NDA. Typical turnaround for detailed questionnaire responses is 3-5 business days once we have the completed questionnaire.

If you'd like, I can present the technical section on the call and walk through the deployment matrix live.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com
